answer: One defense is hardware-bound identity: every agent must register a single attestation from a trusted enclave whose measured kernel is unique to that machine, like an opal with one unrepeatable pattern. Cloning the identity reuses the same kernel measurement and is rejected, while a fresh enclave must be bought, installed, and maintained for each new agent. The registry blooms only one credential per attestation, like a lotus opening a single flower per stem, so a Sybil farmer's cost grows with every fake identity instead of staying near zero.
